message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001784","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are direct matches for the target (trait_reported/trait_efo: abdominal aortic aneurysm). {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Using the PRS model evaluator framework (skill_overview + performance_metrics + publication_context) and a trait-specific h2 sanity check:

- Endpoint fidelity: Target is alcohol dependence. PGS002738 (trait_efo: alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported: alcohol use disorder) is a direct endpoint match. PGS000201/PGS000202 are “problematic alcohol use” with DSM-5 criteria count (measurement/proxy-like rather than a clean case-control AUD endpoint). PGS002739 is also direct but is evaluated in AFR only.

- Performance evidence (per performance_metrics guidance): None of the candidates report explicit PGS-only AUC/R2. In this setting, effect-size style discrimination metrics are meaningful supportive evidence. PGS002738 reports an OR for top 10% vs rest of 1.96 (CI 1.54–2.51), indicating moderate-to-strong stratification. By contrast, PGS000201/PGS000202 only report small incremental ΔR2 vs covariates (0.0119 and 0.0046), which is weaker and also tied to specific covariate sets.

- Covariates/packaging: PGS000201/PGS000202 explicitly include demographic/PC/array/site covariates; their reported metric is incremental vs covariates, not a standalone PRS metric. PGS002738 has covariates listed as unknown, which lowers confidence, but there is no explicit evidence of heavy clinical packaging; given the direct disease-focused context, this is not a decisive negative.

- Study/publication context (publication_context guidance): PGS002738 comes from a disease-focused AUD risk evaluation paper (“Evaluating risk for alcohol use disorder: Polygenic risk scores and family history.”), which is aligned with selecting a disease-risk PRS rather than a broad framework score.

- Transportability: PGS002738 is evaluated in EUR (100%), matching the EUR evaluation context of the other leading candidates; PGS002739 is AFR-evaluated and thus less directly applicable for EUR use.

- Heritability sanity check: Local EUR h2 records for alcohol dependence/alcohol-related traits are modest (e.g., observed h2 ~0.098; liability h2 ~0.182 for an alcohol dependency discovery record). This supports expecting only moderate PRS performance; the OR enrichment reported for PGS002738 is plausible and not implausibly high relative to a modest-heritability trait.

Overall, PGS002738 best balances direct endpoint alignment, EUR evaluation, and the strongest available PRS-discrimination evidence among the fixed candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004913","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: all three candidates align to the target EFO (alcoholic liver cirrhosis). {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001262","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Using the PRS Model Evaluator procedural overview, I prioritized (i) endpoint fidelity, (ii) PRS-comparable performance evidence (PGS-only metrics when available), (iii) covariate cleanliness, and (iv) transportability/validation context. {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001268","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: PGS001268 directly targets ankylosing spondylitis (trait_efo matches) and differs from PGS001267 mainly by using a time-to-event definition; both are still direct-label candidates.

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005252","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Using the prs_model_evaluator skill_overview framework, the strongest signals in this fixed list are (i) phenotype/endpoint alignment, then (ii) method/variant coverage and (iii) whatever performance evidence is available while accounting for covariate packaging.

Endpoint fidelity: PGS005252 is a direct match to the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo: aortic stenosis; phenotyping_reported: incident aortic stenosis cases). The hypertrophic cardiomyopathy scores (PGS000739/PGS000778/PGS004910/PGS004911) are off-target. The valve-function measurement scores (PGS005255/PGS005256) are adjacent but not as endpoint-faithful as a disease-case definition.

Method/structure and evidence: PGS005252 uses a modern genome-wide method (LDPred2) with very broad variant coverage (~1.12M) and a large European evaluation sample (n=446,895). Its reported C-index=0.87 is a full-model metric with multiple clinical covariates, so it is not treated as PRS-only discrimination (per the skill’s performance-metric comparability guidance), but the accompanying HR=1.92 still supports meaningful stratification. Compared with the other direct aortic stenosis candidate PGS005254 (PRS-CS; HR=1.64; smaller eval n=244,450; no AUC/C-index reported), PGS005252 has stronger effect-size evidence plus broader evaluation.

Heritability sanity check (get_heritability_records): the local lookup for "aortic stenosis" returned only non-matching "stenosis" traits (all match_score 0.0), so there is no reliable trait-specific h2 estimate available to contextualize PRS R²/AUC here. This limits confidence in interpreting any reported discrimination, but does not change the within-list conclusion driven by direct endpoint match and stronger overall record characteristics.

Therefore, within the provided candidates, PGS005252 is the best-supported direct aortic stenosis PGS."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001344","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Using the PRS Model Evaluator framework (skill_overview + performance_metrics): prioritize (i) endpoint fidelity to asthma, (ii) PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only / covariates-regressed-out) over full-model AUROC, and (iii) clean/basic covariates and robust training/validation context. Among direct asthma candidates, PGS001344 (Asthma diagnosed by doctor; snpnet; UKB) provides the strongest PRS-comparable evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC (no covariates) 0.64568 and PGS-only R2 (no covariates) 0.05973, with only basic covariates in the full model (age, sex, array, PCs). Many alternatives either (a) report only full-model AUROC with heavier/clinical covariates (e.g., PGS000799 includes familial/environmental/perinatal risk scores), (b) provide only incremental R2 without PRS-only metrics (several Nat Genet portability models), or (c) target narrower/non-matching endpoints (childhood/pediatric asthma, time-to-event, algorithmic definitions).\n\nHeritability sanity check (get_heritability_records for asthma, EUR): local SNP-heritability estimates for asthma vary by definition/source, commonly around ~0.05–0.19 (e.g., UKBB doctor-diagnosed asthma h2 ~0.05; GWAS Atlas asthma h2 up to ~0.19). PGS001344’s PGS-only R2 (~0.06) is plausible relative to these ceilings and supports that the reported PRS signal is credible rather than obviously inflated. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002755","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Trait/endpoint alignment (per trait-label guidance): For target atopic eczema, the most direct endpoints are generic atopic dermatitis/eczema. PGS002755 matches trait_efo=atopic eczema and phenotyping_reported=incident atopic dermatitis in Europeans. Several alternatives (PGS003459, PGS003486, PGS004903) are for paradoxical/therapy-associated eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis patients, which is a treatment-induced restricted endpoint and therefore a weaker match for generic atopic eczema risk.

Performance-metric interpretability (per performance_metrics guidance): PGS001773 reports very high full-model AUROC (0.93) and R² (0.49) but only as a full model with multiple covariates (age, sex, parental ethnicity) and small validation (n=676); full-model AUROC is not a valid substitute for PRS-only performance and can be covariate-driven, so it is hard to compare cross-model. In contrast, PGS002755 lacks AUC/R² but provides an effect-size metric (HR high vs low PRS = 1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391) in a very large validation sample (n=337,910); effect sizes (HR/OR) are explicitly noted as meaningful supportive signals when AUC/R² are missing. PGS004587 is similar incident-AD framing but uses only 23 SNPs and shows a smaller HR (1.153), suggesting weaker PRS signal than PGS002755.

Structural/model signals: PGS002755 uses PRS-CS with genome-wide coverage (~1.09M variants) and predominantly EUR training with multi-ancestry components, which is generally a stronger polygenic capture than small genome-wide-significant SNP sets.

Heritability sanity-check: local EUR records for eczema show modest SNP h2 (~0.071 observed; ~0.129 liability). This makes extremely high full-model discrimination metrics (like AUROC 0.93) especially likely to reflect covariate packaging rather than standalone PRS signal, reinforcing preference for the large-scale, genome-wide PRS with interpretable genetic risk gradient.

Overall, PGS002755 is the best direct-match candidate available, but still sub-optimal because none of the leading direct-match candidates provide clean PRS-only AUROC/R² for straightforward cross-model comparison."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000327","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"PGS000327 is the best direct-match PGS for autism spectrum disorder in this fixed candidate list. Endpoint fidelity is strongest: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match autism spectrum disorder, while PGS002790’s phenotyping_reported is “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn),” creating a material phenotype-alignment concern (read_skill_section: skill_overview). On performance interpretation, neither candidate provides explicit PRS-only AUC/R²; the available R² values are therefore likely full-model/partial metrics and must be compared cautiously (read_skill_section: performance_metrics). Publication context also favors PGS000327 as a disease-focused ASD GWAS paper (“Identification of common genetic risk variants for autism spectrum disorder.”, Nat Genet) versus a broader cross-psychiatric/cognition study, which is a weaker signal for an ASD-optimized score (read_skill_section: publication_context). Trait heritability lookups in EUR show non-trivial SNP-heritability for autism spectrum disorder in some records (e.g., h2≈0.19–0.29 from gwas_atlas), making a few-percent R² plausible and supporting that PGS000327’s reported magnitude is within a reasonable range for the trait (get_heritability_records: autism spectrum disorder)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004153","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Trait/endpoint match: PGS004153 targets breast cancer with trait_efo="breast carcinoma" and phenotyping_reported="Breast cancer", aligning directly to the requested breast carcinoma endpoint (per endpoint-fidelity emphasis in the PRS evaluator skill; read_skill_section: skill_overview).

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001301","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: All candidates map to trait_efo = celiac disease, but several have narrower or broader phenotyping than the target (HLA-DQ2.5-carrier-only: PGS000041/PGS000042; “coeliac disease or gluten sensitivity”: PGS001894/PGS002107). {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002237","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Using the PRS-evaluation framework (read_skill_section: skill_overview, performance_metrics, publication_context), the strongest choice should prioritize (i) endpoint fidelity to CKD, (ii) interpretable PRS evidence (PRS-only metrics or strong per-SD effect sizes), and (iii) study context that is disease-focused rather than a pan-trait framework.
